parameters.content:
## WF3 - Evidence chase (plan section 17)

Polls `GET /cases?state=awaiting_evidence` every 4 hours and, for cases
that have a ready, human-approved evidence-request draft, sends it.

**The biggest honesty note in this whole n8n/ directory.** desk/api.py's
module docstring is explicit that `/cases/<id>/artifacts` -- the endpoint
the original plan assumed this workflow would call to re-ingest a chased
customer's reply -- does not exist. desk/case/state.py's own transition
table (`CASE_TRANSITIONS[CaseState.AWAITING_EVIDENCE] ==
frozenset({CaseState.VERIFYING})`) confirms the *intended* edge is
awaiting_evidence -> verifying, with a source comment attributing it to
"WF3 (plan section 17)" -- so the destination state is real and deliberate,
but nothing in desk/api.py can actually drive a case there today.

**This workflow therefore stops after sending the evidence request.**
Closing the loop -- receiving the customer's reply, feeding the new
artifact back in, and transitioning the case to verifying -- is real,
named future work, not something faked here with a nonexistent endpoint
or a client-side workaround. Until desk/api.py grows that intake path, a
human has to notice the reply and re-run the case manually.

Three more constraints discovered by reading the actual code (not the
original plan draft) shape everything below -- see the sticky notes near
the nodes they explain.

No per-case "last chased" timestamp exists anywhere in desk's data
model or API -- confirmed by reading desk/api.py's full JSON contract
(_case_json / _detail_json). Without one, a workflow that polls every 4
hours and unconditionally sends would re-email the same case every 4
hours for as long as it sits in awaiting_evidence.

The Code node to the right throttles using n8n's own workflow static
data (`$getWorkflowStaticData('global')`), keyed by case id, on a 24h
cadence. This is real n8n functionality, but it is explicitly NOT
authoritative state -- it lives only in this n8n instance's data volume
(ad_n8n_data in compose.yaml) and resets if that volume is lost. desk's
own database has no record of when a case was last chased.

GET /cases/{id}'s own handler comment says `detail` comes from an
**in-process** cache and is null if "the process restarted, or the case
predates this process" (desk/api.py, get_case). It is not durable
storage -- unlike the case's state/disposition, which live in Postgres.

Job B's drafted subject/body and the check gap list both live only
inside `detail`. If the API process has restarted since this case's
pipeline ran, this workflow has no way to know what evidence to ask
for. Rather than guess or send a generic "please resend everything"
message, the false branch below escalates to a human. That matches the
project's own rule that absence of evidence never yields a confident
answer (desk/verify's six-state taxonomy applies the same principle
here, one layer up).

nodes.name: IF detail present and Job B drafted

parameters.subject: =Assertion Desk: case {{ $json.id }} cannot be auto-chased

parameters.content:
Plan section 21 says anything sent to the customer needs approval. WF2
satisfies that by transitioning the case into human_review through
`POST /cases/{id}/post-for-review`. That path is NOT available here --
desk/case/state.py's transition table only allows
awaiting_evidence -> verifying, never awaiting_evidence -> human_review,
so calling post-for-review on one of these cases would 409 for a real
reason, not the benign reason WF2 tolerates.

The send-and-wait node below still puts a human between the draft and
the send, matching the spirit of section 21. But unlike WF2's approval,
this one is NOT recorded in desk's Approval table -- desk/api.py has no
endpoint to approve an evidence-request draft outside a human_review
transition. The approval record lives only in this n8n workflow's own
execution history. Naming that gap here rather than silently accepting
a weaker guarantee than WF2 provides.

parameters.subject: =Assertion Desk: approve evidence request for case {{ $json.id }}

parameters.content:
desk's Case model (and the plan's own section 19 data model) has no
customer-contact field -- confirmed by grepping the whole repo for
customer_email / contact_email / reporter_email, zero hits. Nowhere
records who at the customer's org to reply to. mocks/itsm/ is also
still an empty directory -- the mock ITSM stub the plan names in
section 18/26 as the intended publish target hasn't been built, so
there is no ticket system to post the reply into either.

Plan section 30 is explicit that Gmail here "operates against his own
account for the demo only," never real outbound mail to a real
customer. In keeping with that, the send below targets a configurable
demo address, not an address extracted from the case. Wiring a real
customer-contact field into desk's data model and a real ITSM publish
path are both genuine future work, not faked here.
